answer: Forced-Divergence Route Sampling: each identity must commit daily to one route through a seeded environment whose hidden structure (an oasis somewhere, a karst channel elsewhere) is revealed only after commitment. Honest operators update routes from that feedback, so their next commitments drift; clones sharing one mind cannot diverge without splitting their payoff. Each clone must therefore pay a separate exploration cost every tide of the schedule, and the cost compounds per copy since divergence forfeits shared learning.
